fundamentals.name: Lennar Corporation
fundamentals.longBusinessSummary: Lennar Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, operates as a homebuilder primarily under the Lennar brand in the United States. It operates through Homebuilding East, Homebuilding Central, Homebuilding South Central, Homebuilding West, Financial Services, Multifamily, and Lennar Other segments. The company's homebuilding operations include the construction and sale of single-family attached and detached homes, as well as the purchase, development, and sale of residential land; and development, construction, and management of multifamily rental properties. It also offers residential mortgage financing, title insurance, and closing services for home buyers and others, as well as originating and selling securitization commercial mortgage loans. In addition, the company is involved in fund investment activities. It primarily serves first-time, move-up, active adult, and luxury homebuyers. The company was founded in 1954 and is based in Miami, Florida.

judgment.summary: Lennar shows a strong balance sheet and cash flow but faces significant headwinds from declining revenue and earnings growth.
judgment.earningsRecap: Last quarter missed EPS estimates; next earnings date is 2026-06-11.
positives: Trailing P/E of 13.02 and forward P/E of 11.98 suggest a reasonable valuation.
PEG ratio of 0.77 indicates potential for growth relative to its price.
Strong current ratio (8.33) and quick ratio (3.54) point to excellent short-term liquidity.
Total cash ($8.98B) significantly exceeds total debt ($5.51B), resulting in positive net cash.
Free cash flow (TTM) of $3.44B is robust.
Dividend yield of 2.2% with a conservative payout ratio (28.8%) offers income.
negatives: Revenue growth YoY is negative at -13.3%.
Earnings growth YoY is significantly negative at -52.6%.
Quarterly earnings growth shows a steep decline of -55.8%.
Analyst growth estimates for the current quarter (-34.5%) and fiscal year (-26.0%) are also negative.
Operating margin (3.6%) and profit margin (5.4%) are relatively thin.
Return on equity (8.1%) and return on assets (4.3%) are modest.

news.paragraph: Lennar is approaching its Q2 earnings print with a mixed sentiment, as some analysts are buying ahead of the report while others note the struggles of the U.S. housing market. Recent articles highlight both potential opportunities and the headwinds facing homebuilders, with charts suggesting a possible rebound. The company's stock has underperformed the market recently, but some see value emerging.
